title: Handoff + Escalation: Dedicated GPU Capacity (scratchpad)
content:
Context / purpose:
- Prep for 1:1 with CapEx ops and weekly capacity sync (Thu). Focus: reduce friction in handoff when pool pressure spikes; establish clear escalation steps and temporary reservation patterns to avoid priority inversion for customer SLAs.
- This is a personal scratchpad to shape an agenda and capture action items; will convert to a short runbook blurb after next sync.

Attendees to invite (compact list):
- Evan (capacity ops) -- main owner for reservations
- Jules (SRE lead) -- affects on-call and escalation
- Priya (Billing/FinOps) -- need quick cost ack for emergency bursts
- Samir (product-hosted-api) -- customer impact perspective
- Me (Maya) -- shepherd decisions and follow-through

Quick snapshot (numbers to confirm before meeting):
- Committed GPUs (monthly reserved): 480 v100-equivalent (current commit)
- Active pool running: 420 GPUs
- Average steady util (last 7d): 73% overall; peak 92% (4h window)
- Autoscale headroom configured: +20% burst via preemptible/spot (policy A)
- Pending reservations request: INF-4821 -> +64 GPUs for Apr-May trial
- Budget guardrail for bursts this quarter: $75k discretionary (Priya to confirm)

Open questions to answer in sync (ranked):
1) What is the minimum lead time needed to convert a short-term reservation into a committed monthly pool without breaking billing cycles? (Ops)
2) How long for infra to make +10% capacity available in another region (eu-west) if ap-south saturates? (Infra)
3) Are there safe, pre-authorized thresholds where SRE can trigger an emergency top-up (spot -> reserved bridge) without exec approval?
4) Do we have automated signals that classify load as "realtime latency-sensitive" vs "batch/embeddings" for policy routing? (Product)

Agenda draft (20–30 min):
- 0–5m: current numbers + last incident recap (who paged, what happened)
- 5–12m: decision items: short-term reservation (INF-4821) + emergency top-up criteria
- 12–20m: autoscale policy tweak proposals (thresholds, cooldowns, cost ceilings)
- 20–30m: handoff + communication template (who notifies customers, Slack + pager text)

Incident vignette (recent):
- 2025-02-12 14:10 UTC: sudden spike from a new enterprise customer test; autoscale filled spot pool then hit priority queue. Result: 45s median latency -> 270ms -> 1.1s for top tier route; external SLA flag raised. Root cause: request burst pattern + model variant fallback misconfigured (old variant non-quantized took longer).
- Lessons: fallback/variant mapping needs stricter latency guardrails; allow temporary reservation conversion for the affected customer route to avoid cascading retries.

Decision proposals (short bullets):
- Proposal A (conservative): Pre-authorize SRE to request emergency +8% reserved capacity for up to 72 hours via a one-click approval in the capacity console; requires immediate notification to FinOps and capacity ops.
- Proposal B (cost-first): Increase spot buffer to +30% and lower cooldown to 60s, but limit to non-SLA customers.
- Proposal C (route isolation): Temporarily isolate high-latency-prone routes onto dedicated small pools (8–16 GPUs) to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Runbook / Handoff checklist (quick steps for on-call to follow):
1) Confirm pool metrics (util, queue depth, avg latency) and tag event severity (sev1 if median latency >500ms for 5m on SLA routes).
2) Open an incident in PagerDuty and post to #capacity-ops with the incident template (below).
3) If severity rules met, trigger emergency conversion flow (if pre-authorized) or open request for +reservation (INF-xxxx) with "urgent" tag.
4) If conversion accepted, monitor cost burn in FinOps dashboard and set daily check-ins until normalized.
5) After event, capture timeline + decisions in postmortem and update this scratchpad.

Slack + pager templates (copy-ready):
- Slack (channel #capacity-ops):
  "INCIDENT: high latency on hosted-api route /model/X. Median latency 820ms over 6m. Queue depth 240. Paging SRE + Capacity Ops. @Evan_P please check pool saturation and consider emergency +reservation. Ticket: INF-XXXX"
- Pager (short):
  "Capacity Sev1: /model/X high latency; check pool util & consider emergency reservation. PD link: <link>"

Back-of-envelope cost calc (green light thresholds):
- Marginal cost per reserved v100 GPU per day (estimate): $16
- Emergency +64 GPUs for 3 days = 64 * 3 * $16 = $3,072 (within $75k discretionary)
- If we convert to monthly commit mid-month, pro-rated incremental commitment ~ $12k (finance calc needed)

Routing / autoscale heuristics to propose:
- Keep latency-sensitive routes on smaller pools with stricter cool-down (90s) and a lower CPU/KV cache warmup policy.
- For embeddings/batch: increase batching factor and allow slower cooldown (5m) to save cost.
- Signal-based autoscale triggers: queue depth + percentile latency + recent model change flag. Use a weighted score (0-100) where >70 => scale up.

Outstanding tickets / follow-ups to list in meeting: (owner -> todo -> due)
- INF-4821 (Evan) -> finalize +64 GPU trial request; provide billing estimate (due 2025-02-21)
- INF-4978 (Jules) -> add route classification labels to tracing pipeline (due 2025-03-04)
- PR #329 (Samir) -> small change to model-variant fallback thresholds (merge after tests) (due 2025-02-20)
- New runbook stub (Maya) -> draft post-incident handoff doc and share (due 2025-02-26)

Action items (clear owners and dates):
- Maya: email Priya + attach cost calc for emergency bursts; ask for confirmed discretionary cap (due 2025-02-19).
- Evan: prepare quick checklist for one-click reservation conversion UI and requirements for audit trail (due 2025-02-21).
- Jules: simulate a 10% sudden load test in staging and capture cooldown behavior (due 2025-02-25).
- Samir: flag product routes that are allowed to run on spot-heavy pools (due 2025-02-22).

Notes to self (scratchy):
- Keep this doc focused on handoff (not policy debates). We can spin a separate doc for long-term commit strategy.
- After next sync: convert the Slack/pager templates into templates in PD (incidents) and add to Confluence runbook.
- Check whether we can automate the "cost ack" step in the UI (small checkbox that notifies FinOps) -> reduces friction.

Quick SQL / queries to run before meeting (placeholders):
- SELECT pool, avg(util), p95(latency), queue_depth FROM capacity_metrics WHERE timestamp > now()-interval '7 days' GROUP BY pool;
- SELECT route, count(*) FROM served_requests WHERE status = 'retry' AND timestamp > now()-interval '1 day' GROUP BY route;

Next meeting: Thu weekly capacity sync (2025-02-20) 10:00 PST. Prepare 2 slides: 1) what happened + current numbers; 2) proposed decision and action list.

Appendix / quick refs:
- Post-incident notes link (will create)
- Capacity console -> reservations -> precommit UI screenshots (ask Evan to attach)
- Priority routes list: hosted-api:/chat, hosted-api:/embeddings, dedicated-customer-A (private)

-- end scratchpad --
